passage:
A museum introduced an app that let visitors scan objects and hear stories in different languages. Many visitors enjoyed it because they could move at their own speed.
But the museum noticed a problem. Some people looked only at their phones and barely looked at the objects.
The museum changed the app. Before each story played, it asked visitors to look at the object for ten seconds and notice one detail.
The change worked. Visitors became more focused.
The museum learned that digital guides should not pull attention away from the real thing. Good technology should lead eyes back to the world, not trap them on a screen.
